# retro-skill

LLM-driven session retrospection skill. Detects friction in agent sessions and materializes learnings into correct destinations.

## Structure

- `skills/retro/SKILL.md` — Main skill definition (sweep, spotlight, outcome, audit, promote, done, auto modes)
- `skills/retro/checkpoints.yaml` — Skill quality gates
- `commands/retro.md` — `/retro` slash command definition
- `hooks/session-end.json` — Optional SessionEnd hook: prints a reminder to run `/retro`, does not invoke it (off by default)
- `skills/retro/references/` — Friction catalog, destination taxonomy, classification heuristic, skill discovery, documentation lookup, patch workflow, eval integration, workflow modes
- `skills/retro/scripts/detect-mechanical.py` — Schicht-A pre-pass (mechanical friction detection)
- `skills/retro/scripts/mask-secrets.py` — Credential masking that `detect-mechanical.py`, `scan-cross-session.py`, `derive-session-scope.py`, `collect-review-findings.py` and `scan-memory-inventory.py` apply to the text they quote (not a command)
- `skills/retro/scripts/opencode-transcript.py` — Renders an opencode session (SQLite) as the JSONL Schicht A reads
- `skills/retro/scripts/codex-transcript.py` — Renders a Codex CLI rollout as the JSONL Schicht A reads; real excerpts in `tests/fixtures/codex/`
- `skills/retro/scripts/collect-session-metrics.py` — Normalizes recorded usage, observed time and provenance; unknown costs and parent/child counter overlap remain explicit
- `skills/retro/scripts/find-org-skills.py` — Skill discovery: every marketplace skill, installed or not
- `skills/retro/scripts/find-installed-skills.sh` — Installed-only detail (paths, git remotes)
- `skills/retro/scripts/scan-cross-session.py` — Cross-session JSONL scanner (Schicht-C)
- `skills/retro/references/prior-attempts.md` — Find previous interventions through scoped memories, session indexes and original records
- `skills/retro/scripts/orca-search-refs.jq` — Reduce Orca search output to session references and page coverage
- `skills/retro/scripts/collect-review-findings.py` — Review threads, bot reviews, native issue comments and supplied tracker feedback on the PRs/MRs a session wrote to (input for B18–B20, D4, D6); takes the artefact list from `derive-session-scope.py`
- `skills/retro/scripts/feedback-contract.py` — Validates local, tracker-neutral feedback; no discovery or execution
- `skills/retro/scripts/scan-memory-inventory.py` — Promote-mode pre-pass over the memory backlog
- `skills/retro/scripts/check-upstream-sources.py` — Drift check against canonical sources
- `skills/retro/scripts/check-decision-records.py` — Reads the ADR declaration of a root `AGENTS.md` and the `Touches` anchors of decision records (E1, E7, E8)
- `skills/retro/scripts/materialize-pr.sh` — Opens the skill-update PR against the source repo
- `skills/retro/scripts/validate-evals.py` — Validates retro's own eval scenarios (RT-40..42)
- `skills/retro/scripts/prepare-behavior-evals.py` — Freezes selected Markdown scenarios for native execution or the shared runner, with private grading inputs and isolated old/new fixtures
- `skills/retro/scripts/check-eval-samples.py` — Refuses an eval retro adds or tightens without `samples` (called by `materialize-pr.sh finish`)
- `skills/retro/evals/` — retro's own classification evals (LLM-graded fixtures; see `skills/retro/evals/README.md`)
- `docs/specs/retro-skill.md` — Original spec, superseded (header says why); kept as a historical record

## Commands

- `/retro` — Sweep: analyze entire current session
- `/retro "<problem>"` — Spotlight: focus on specific issue
- `/retro outcome [session-id|--since N]` — Outcome: post-hoc review of a past session
- `/retro audit [--scope project|repo|skill]` — Audit: cross-session architectural review
- `/retro promote` — Promote: re-home accumulated local memory upward
- `/retro done` — Done: eight-gate definition-of-done check (task, findings, retro, cleanup, questions, tickets, time, docs)

## Rules

- LLM is primary classifier; mechanical pre-pass reduces token cost but does not classify
- Patches always go to source repo, never to local cache
- Verify authorization for each target, action and audience, including private repositories; reuse permission already granted for that scope
- Execute already authorized materializations and report them; ask only for uncovered decisions, without repeating approval requests
- Rule purpose precedes enforcement: consider removal, simplification and tool/environment changes before adding a gate
- Original task completion and later benefit are separate; a justified no-op and an untested future effect are valid outcomes
- No auto-merge; no continuous background hooks (except optional SessionEnd)
- Tracker-neutral core: no implicit tracker, external CLI discovery or organization billing policy; see `skills/retro/references/feedback-contract.md`
- A transcript adapter (`*-transcript.py`) is checked against sessions a real CLI wrote, not only hand-built rows: its docstring names the CLI versions measured, and either its tests carry a redacted excerpt of a real session or a `docs/` page records the live check, as [opencode live test](docs/opencode-live-test.md) does. Hand-built rows for one shape left every tool call of the other shapes unconverted in #168

## Key Decisions

- **ADRs:** yes — `docs/adr/` ([how to write one](docs/adr/AGENTS.md))

## Relationships

- `agent-harness-skill` — verifies integration points (PR retro question, optional SessionEnd hook)
- `agent-rules-skill` — defines the `AGENTS.md` conventions that project-rule materialization writes to
- `skill-repo-skill` — defines PR/branch convention for skill-update materialization
- `automated-assessment-skill` — defines YAML schema for checkpoint materialization

## See also

- [Spec](docs/specs/retro-skill.md) — Original specification, superseded; historical record
- [opencode live test](docs/opencode-live-test.md) — Checking `opencode-transcript.py` against a real, isolated opencode 2.x

# ADR-001: Declare decision records in AGENTS.md and anchor them by path

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-11-22
**Touches:** `skills/retro/scripts/check-decision-records.py`, `skills/retro/references/destination-taxonomy.md`, `AGENTS.md`

## Context

Retro routes decisions to project rules, but a project's `AGENTS.md` often
does not say whether it keeps ADRs or where. A decision then lands in a
commit, a comment or nowhere, and a later session cannot find it. A review of
trailhq/Trail-Code, which binds learnings to code paths, raised the question
of what retro should take over.

## Decision

- The root `AGENTS.md` of a project states `**ADRs:** yes — <directory>` or
  `**ADRs:** no — <place>` in its Key Decisions. A missing or contradicted
  declaration is a finding (E7). Retro never picks the place; the project
  owner decides yes or no.
- With `yes`, the directory has its own `AGENTS.md` that says how records
  are written.
- A record names the paths it governs in `**Touches:**`. Retro reports
  anchors that are gone (E8) and changes below an anchor (E1, a candidate
  until the record is read).
- retro-skill itself keeps ADRs in `docs/adr/`.

## Ruled out

- **Matching names in a record's prose against the code.** Trail-Code
  measured this and recorded that 9 of the 10 learnings it flagged still
  matched the code (learning `l-3cfeb3b1`).
- **A pre-PR conflict check inside retro.** Retro runs after a session. The
  check before a pull request belongs to the repository's CI, owned by
  agent-harness-skill.
- **YAML frontmatter as the only record form.** The ADRs read in two
  organisation repositories use bold fields; the reader accepts both.

## Consequences

- Existing ADRs without `**Touches:**` are reported as unanchored, not as
  findings, so E1 and E8 apply only to records written with anchors.
- agent-rules-skill has to write the declaration when it generates an
  `AGENTS.md`, and agent-harness-skill has to enforce it.

# Decision records

This directory holds the decision records (ADRs) of retro-skill. The root
`AGENTS.md` declares it with `**ADRs:** yes`, and
`skills/retro/scripts/check-decision-records.py` reads both.

## When a decision needs a record

Write a record when a change chooses between options that a later change
could reverse without knowing why: a routing rule, a script's contract, a
signal's meaning, a measured limit. A wording fix or a single bug fix needs
none; its pull request is its record.

## Form

One file per decision, `ADR-NNN-<slug>.md`, numbered in order. Use the bold
fields below, then the sections:

```markdown
# ADR-NNN: <Title>

**Status:** Proposed | Accepted | Superseded by ADR-NNN
**Date:** YYYY-MM-DD
**Touches:** `path/one`, `dir/`

## Context
## Decision
## Ruled out
## Consequences
```

- `**Touches:**` names the files, directories or globs the decision governs.
  `check-decision-records.py` reports a named path that is gone (E8) and a
  change below one (E1).
- `## Ruled out` names the options that were rejected and why.

## Changing a decision

Never edit an accepted record. Write a new record that states the new
decision and its reason, and set the old record's status to
`Superseded by ADR-NNN`. A typo, a broken link or a `**Touches:**` path
that moved with its code may be fixed in place.
